learning_outcomes.text: Understand the criteria that establish the classical elasticity limit, the behavior of materials in elasto-plastic regimes, and the constitutive equations that determine this relationship.
Analyze the response of advanced materials that incorporate viscous behavior, both viscoelastic and viscoplastic.

Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve calculation and design problems for components that require incorporating the inelastic behavior of materials, using specifically established methods.
Be able to apply both analytical and numerical solution methods in solving structural problems with visco-elasto-plastic materials.
Be able to apply the acquired knowledge to interpret experimental results, and to carry out designs of structural components that meet specific requirements.
Understand and appropriately use the different methods that exist to characterize and analyze the mechanical response of materials with visco-elasto-plastic behavior.
Be able to design and conduct experiments for the characterization of inelastic materials, as well as interpret data and draw conclusions.
Acquire technical and laboratory competencies.
Be able to select and use appropriate tools and methods to characterize materials with visco-elasto-plastic behavior.
Acquire the ability to combine theoretical concepts and practical exercises to solve problems involving mechanical and/or structural components where inelastic materials are required.

Understand the methods, both analytical and numerical, used in the characterization and analysis of visco-elasto-plastic solid behavior, being aware of existing limitations, mainly from an analytical point of view.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
Adequate knowledge of their engineering branch, including some cutting-edge knowledge in their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competencies.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
Understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering, to meet required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Mechanical Behavior of Materials
The Equations of Solid Mechanics. Kinematics of Deformable Solids
Equations of Plasticity. Incremental Theory of Plasticity.
The Finite Element Method in Plasticity.
Viscoelastic constitutive models based on linear analogies
Viscoplastic constitutive models based on non-linear analogies
Introduction to Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics.

assessment_methods.method: Assignments, class participation, and partial tests (part of Continuous Assessment)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 60% from the Final Exam and 40% from Continuous Assessment, which includes lab practices (15% of total) and other components (25% of total). A minimum grade of 4.5 in the Final Exam is required for the Continuous Assessment to be considered. Attendance and completion of lab practices are mandatory to pass the course. The use of artificial intelligence tools for assignments or exercises is prohibited and will be considered academic fraud.
